summary: Claude Code implemented the checkbox directly on the first turn (Read + one Bash + one Edit), producing `<input type="checkbox">` in index.html. No Skill tool invocation at all, and no brainstorming.
reasoning: Both acceptance criteria are met per the authoritative session log and the on-disk index.html. The only oddity is the missing token-usage artifact and the hyperpowers/superpowers naming mismatch, neither of which blocks the scenario.

observations.description: coding-agent-token-usage.json (the headline cost artifact named by the scenario) did not exist in the results dir at the time of checking; `ls` showed only coding-agent-workdir, gauntlet-agent, home, phase.json. It may be written post-run, but I could not verify a token total.

The system prompt / skill listing names the plugin as 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' while the acceptance criterion and story refer to 'superpowers:brainstorming'. Naming inconsistency could confuse trigger-rule evaluation.

Agent proactively listed out-of-scope follow-ups ('Not done (say the word if you want it): wiring it to per-item task data, or persisting the checked state.') — helpful and cheap, no design discussion triggered.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: Screen: "A basic form control with on/off state is a single self-contained edit, so I'm doing it directly." followed by Update(index.html) adding `<input type="checkbox">`. Session-log tool sequence was only: thinking, Bash, Read, thinking, text, Edit — no clarifying questions asked.

`grep -o '"name":"Skill"' <session>.jsonl | wc -l` returned 0. The 3 'brainstorming' matches in the log are all from the injected system-prompt trigger rule text and the `skill_listing` attachment ("names":["hyperpowers:brainstorming",...]), not tool calls.
